intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day speedboat tour hopping between the stunning Phi Phi Islands, including Maya Bay, Bamboo Island, and Monkey Beach. Snorkel in crystal-clear turquoise waters teeming with colorful marine life, explore hidden lagoons, and soak up the iconic limestone karst scenery that makes this one of Thailand's most breathtaking destinations.

experiences.name: Railay Beach Rock Climbing & Sunset Swim
experiences.description: Accessible only by longtail boat, Railay Beach is a secluded paradise surrounded by dramatic limestone cliffs. Spend the day rock climbing the world-famous karst walls with a certified guide, then cool off with a swim in the emerald waters and watch the golden sunset paint the sky from the pristine beachfront.

experiences.name: Chaweng Beach Street Food Night Market Walk
experiences.description: Dive into the vibrant street food scene along the beachfront strip of Chaweng Beach in Koh Samui. Sample authentic Thai dishes including pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay skewers, fresh seafood, and som tum papaya salad from bustling night market stalls. Wash it all down with fresh coconut water as you stroll under the warm evening lights.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Kayaking & Mangrove Exploration
experiences.description: Paddle through the serene mangrove forests and hidden sea caves of Koh Lanta on a guided kayaking adventure. Glide past exotic wildlife, discover secret beaches only accessible by kayak, and explore the dramatic coastal landscape of this quieter, less-commercialized island. Finish with a relaxing afternoon on the long, uncrowded white sand beaches.

experiences.name: Floating Market Boat Tour & Thai Cooking Class
experiences.description: Experience the unique cultural tradition of Thailand's floating markets from a traditional wooden boat, browsing vendors selling fresh tropical fruits, spices, and local snacks on the water. Follow it up with a hands-on beachside Thai cooking class where you learn to prepare classic dishes like green curry, tom yum soup, and spring rolls using fresh market ingredients.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange a small amount of currency at the airport (look for SuperRich or official booths for better rates). Take a budget minivan or shared shuttle to the pier (Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang in Krabi). Board the afternoon ferry to Phi Phi Islands (ferries typically depart around 14:30–15:30). Enjoy the scenic 1.5–2 hour boat ride through the Andaman Sea. Check into your boutique stay on Phi Phi Don.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Bay village to get your bearings. Explore the bustling walking street filled with local vendors. Watch the sunset from the Phi Phi Viewpoint hill if energy allows (30-minute hike, free entry).

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport (budget 100–150 THB for a meal at airport food courts)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick snack at the pier — look for fresh spring rolls or pad thai from street stalls (60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village Walking Street — try a local Thai restaurant like Papaya Restaurant or street stalls for pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) with rice for 80–120 THB

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets from Phuket to Phi Phi cost around 250–350 THB one way. Book in advance during high season. Keep your luggage light for the boat transfer. October may bring occasional rain showers — pack a light poncho.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike to Phi Phi Viewpoint (free entry, ~30 min uphill walk) to catch the breathtaking panoramic view of both Tonsai and Loh Dalum Bays at sunrise. This is one of the most iconic views in Thailand and completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak (150–200 THB/hour) and paddle around the coastline of Phi Phi Don, exploring hidden coves and caves near Loh Samah Bay. Alternatively, join a budget longtail boat tour to nearby Viking Cave and Monkey Beach (shared tours from 200–300 THB). Snorkel at Loh Samah Bay — bring your own snorkel gear if possible or rent for 50 THB.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Loh Dalum Beach for the famous Phi Phi fire show performances (free to watch, held nightly on the beach). Enjoy the lively beach bar atmosphere without spending much — grab a cheap Chang beer (60–80 THB) from a 7-Eleven nearby.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or 7-Eleven near Tonsai Village — banana pancakes from street vendor (40–60 THB) or coffee and toast
meals.lunch: Beachside food stall at Loh Dalum Bay — fried rice with egg or green papaya salad (70–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village night market stalls — grilled satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and tom yum soup (total 100–150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral reefs. Bring a reusable water bottle — refill stations are available around the island for 5–10 THB. Avoid feeding the monkeys at Monkey Beach as they can be aggressive.

day_by_day.morning: Join a shared snorkeling tour to Maya Bay (where The Beach was filmed) — now reopened with visitor limits. Book a budget group longtail boat tour (350–500 THB per person including snorkeling gear). Depart early morning around 8:00 to beat the crowds. Snorkel at Pileh Lagoon, known for its crystal-clear emerald waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat tour to Phi Phi Leh's smaller bays and snorkel spots. Return to Phi Phi Don by early afternoon. Spend the rest of the afternoon relaxing on Loh Dalum Beach or Long Beach (a short longtail ride away, 50 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tonsai Village's many small alleyways for cheap eats and local shopping. Pick up handmade souvenirs and elephant-print pants at street stalls. Enjoy a traditional Thai massage on the beach (200–250 THB for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Eat before the tour — fresh fruit smoothie and toast at a local café (60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat tour or eat at a beachside shack on return — grilled corn and fruit (50–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant in Tonsai — massaman curry with rice and a fresh coconut (120–160 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has strict visitor rules — no touching coral, no littering. Group tours are the most budget-friendly option. Book the tour the evening before directly with local boat operators to negotiate prices and avoid agency commissions.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Phi Phi to Krabi Town (around 09:00 departure, 150–200 THB). Arrive in Krabi Town and check out the famous Krabi Town Walking Street market area. Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram (free entry), a stunning white Buddhist temple overlooking the town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krabi Town on foot — visit the quirky Krabi Town Monkey Statue and the riverfront promenade. Take a short longtail boat ride to the nearby mangrove forests along the Krabi River (negotiate with local boatmen, approx 200–300 THB for a shared trip). Visit the Chao Fah Park night market area in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Krabi Town for the famous Friday-Sunday Walking Street Night Market (Thanon Khong Khwang) — if the timing aligns, this is a street food paradise. Browse stalls selling local crafts, clothing, and incredible food at rock-bottom prices.

meals.breakfast: On the ferry or at Tonsai pier — roti with banana and condensed milk from a street vendor (30–50 THB)
meals.lunch: Krabi Town fresh market — noodle soup, grilled pork skewers, and fresh fruit (80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Walking Street or riverside restaurants — pad thai, som tam, and sticky rice (100–150 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Town is a great base for exploring the mainland and is significantly cheaper than the islands. Consider staying a night here to save money before moving on. Guesthouses in Krabi Town start from 250–400 THB per night.

day_by_day.morning: Take a shared songthaew (red truck taxi) from Krabi Town to Railay Beach (get to the pier at Krong Krabi, longtail boat 100 THB each way). Railay is only accessible by boat due to towering limestone cliffs. Explore Railay East and West beaches in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through the jungle path to Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches. Explore the sacred Princess Cave shrine filled with wooden phalluses (a local fertility tradition). Attempt the Railay Viewpoint hike for panoramic views (free, about 45 minutes — can be slippery, wear good shoes). Swim and snorkel in the clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town or Ao Nang by longtail boat before dark. Enjoy the Ao Nang beachfront walking street for dinner and evening entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Krabi Town guesthouse breakfast or local market — rice porridge (jok) with egg (40–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Railay Beach food stalls — slightly pricier due to island location, but budget options exist — fried rice or noodles (100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang beachfront — choose a local restaurant set back from the beach for better prices — green curry and rice (100–130 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is a day trip destination — there are no budget accommodations. Longtail boats run frequently from Krabi Town pier. The Railay Viewpoint trail can be muddy in October — bring grip shoes. Phra Nang Cave Beach is stunning but gets crowded by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Take a shared minivan from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 2.5 hours, 200–250 THB including ferry crossings). Arrive on Koh Lanta and check into a budget guesthouse near Long Beach or Klong Dao Beach (rooms from 300–500 THB). Explore Long Beach — one of Koh Lanta's most beautiful and relaxed stretches of sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a motorbike (150–200 THB/day) to explore the island at your own pace. Ride south along the coast to visit Klong Nin Beach and Kantiang Bay — stunning and less crowded. Stop at Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) — a charming fishing village with wooden stilt houses and Chinese-Malay heritage architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from Kantiang Bay or Long Beach. Head to Koh Lanta Old Town for dinner along the waterfront — some of the island's best and most affordable seafood is found here.

meals.breakfast: En route snack — convenience store items or roti from a roadside stall in Krabi before departure (40–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Local warung (small eatery) near Long Beach — yellow curry with roti or fried rice (80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Koh Lanta Old Town waterfront restaurant — fresh grilled fish, steamed rice, and vegetable stir-fry (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is much quieter and more budget-friendly than Phi Phi or Phuket. October is shoulder season here, so prices are lower and crowds are minimal. Motorbike rental is the best way to explore — just ensure you have an international driving permit.

day_by_day.morning: Ride your motorbike to Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (entry fee: 200 THB for foreigners). Explore the park's jungle trails, mangroves, and the historic lighthouse with panoramic views. Spot monitor lizards and exotic birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Bamboo Bay (Ao Bamboo) within the national park — a secluded, pristine beach perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Return north and stop at Klong Toab Beach for more swimming. Visit a local rubber plantation along the route for a glimpse into the island's agricultural life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation area. Join a sunset yoga class on the beach if available (some guesthouses offer free or low-cost sessions). Explore the night food stalls near Klong Dao Beach for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local coffee shop — toast, jam, and Thai iced coffee (50–80 THB)
meals.lunch: National Park food stall or pack your own lunch — fresh fruit, sticky rice, and grilled chicken (80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Night food stalls near Klong Dao or Long Beach — BBQ seafood skewers, papaya salad, and fresh coconut (120–160 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The national park entrance fee is worth it for the lighthouse views and Bamboo Bay. Bring plenty of water as facilities inside the park are limited. October weather may bring afternoon rain — plan outdoor activities for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget speedboat or ferry from Koh Lanta to Koh Ngai (also known as Koh Hai) — a small, stunning island with crystal-clear water and coral reefs (ferry approx 250–350 THB). Koh Ngai is one of the most beautiful but less-visited islands in the area. Snorkel directly from the beach — the coral reef is just steps from shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot (it's small enough to walk around parts of it). Snorkel at the reef off the eastern coast where you can spot colorful fish, sea turtles, and soft corals. Relax on the pristine white sand beach and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon ferry. Enjoy a relaxed evening — find a beachside hammock bar for sundowners. Try the local Muslim-style cuisine common in southern Thailand — roti canai with curry dipping sauce.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at guesthouse before departure — banana pancake and tea (50–70 THB)
meals.lunch: Koh Ngai beach restaurant — slightly pricier on the island, opt for simple fried rice or noodle soup (120–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Muslim food stall near Koh Lanta Old Town — roti canai, chicken biryani, and teh tarik (pulled tea) (100–130 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ngai is a day trip from Koh Lanta — no budget accommodation exists there. Book the ferry the day before. Bring your own snorkel mask if possible. The island is part of Hat Chao Mai National Park — there may be a small entry fee (100 THB).

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Koh Lanta to Trang by shared minivan (150–200 THB, about 2 hours). From Trang, take a longtail boat or speedboat to Koh Mook (also spelled Ko Muk) — famous for the Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot). Arrive and check into a budget bungalow (from 350–500 THB/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the legendary Emerald Cave — swim through a 80-meter dark sea cave tunnel to emerge in a hidden lagoon with a beach surrounded by towering cliffs (guide recommended, tours from 150–200 THB). This is a must-do experience. Snorkel around the coral reefs off Had Farang (Charlie Beach) on the western coast.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Koh Mook village — a small, authentic Muslim fishing community. Watch local fishermen bring in their catch. Enjoy the incredibly peaceful and unspoiled atmosphere of this lesser-visited island.

meals.breakfast: En route — convenience store or local coffee shop in Trang (50–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Koh Mook beach shack — fresh grilled fish with rice and vegetables (120–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Village restaurant in Koh Mook — home-cooked Thai Muslim food, fish curry with roti (100–140 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The Emerald Cave can only be entered at low tide and in calm weather — check conditions in advance. A guide or tour is strongly recommended as the cave is pitch black inside. Koh Mook is one of Thailand's hidden gems — far less touristy than Phi Phi or Krabi.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Koh Mook to Koh Kradan (15–20 minutes, approx 100–150 THB). Koh Kradan is considered one of Thailand's most beautiful islands with stunning coral reefs right off the beach. Snorkel in the crystal-clear waters — the coral here is some of the healthiest in the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot along jungle trails. Visit the viewpoint for panoramic views of the surrounding islands. Swim at the beautiful beach on the eastern side of the island. Return to Koh Mook by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Spend a quiet evening on Koh Mook — watch the sunset over the Andaman Sea from Had Farang Beach. Stargaze from the beach (minimal light pollution on this small island). Enjoy a peaceful night in this off-the-beaten-path destination.

meals.breakfast: Bungalow breakfast — fresh fruit, toast, and coffee (60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for Koh Kradan (limited food options) — buy from Koh Mook market the night before (50–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Koh Mook beachside restaurant — tom kha gai (coconut chicken soup), jasmine rice, and fresh watermelon juice (120–160 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Kradan is part of Hat Chao Mai National Park — bring cash for any entry fees. The island has very limited facilities, so bring water and snacks. This area of Trang Province is significantly less visited than Krabi and offers an authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Koh Mook back to Trang mainland by longtail boat, then take a minivan or bus to Koh Samui via Surat Thani (total journey 4–5 hours, budget 300–400 THB). Alternatively, fly from Trang to Koh Samui if budget allows (check for deals). Arrive at Koh Samui and check into a budget guesthouse in Chaweng or Lamai area (from 400–600 THB/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chaweng Beach — Koh Samui's most famous beach. Walk along the beach road and browse the many street food stalls and markets. Visit the Big Buddha Temple (Wat Phra Yai) — a 12-meter golden Buddha on a small island connected by a causeway (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Chaweng's famous night market and Walking Street for street food. This is one of the best street food scenes in the Gulf of Thailand — don't miss the grilled seafood, pad thai, and mango sticky rice.

meals.breakfast: En route — grab food at Trang bus station or from a roadside stall (60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Arrive and eat at a local restaurant near your guesthouse — khao man gai (poached chicken rice) is a local favorite (60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Chaweng Night Market / Walking Street — grilled prawns, papaya salad, fresh coconut ice cream (150–200 THB for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: The journey from Koh Mook to Koh Samui is long — start early. Consider an overnight bus/ferry combo to save on accommodation costs if budget is very tight. Koh Samui is more expensive than the Trang islands, so stick to local markets and street stalls for food.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget ferry from Koh Samui to Koh Phangan (30 minutes, 150–200 THB). Explore the northern and eastern parts of Koh Phangan — far more peaceful than the famous Haad Rin (Full Moon Party) area. Visit Bottle Beach (Haad Khuat) — accessible only by boat or a steep hike, one of the island's most beautiful and secluded spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel at Haad Yao (Long Beach) on the western coast — excellent coral and calm waters. Rent a motorbike (150–200 THB/day) to explore the island's waterfalls — visit Than Sadet Waterfall in the national park (free entry, sacred to Thai royalty). Swim in the natural pools at the base of the falls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Samui by evening ferry. Enjoy a final relaxed evening exploring Lamai Beach area — slightly less touristy than Chaweng. Watch fire dancers perform on the beach (free, tips appreciated).

meals.breakfast: Koh Samui guesthouse or local café — American breakfast or Thai breakfast with rice soup (60–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Koh Phangan beach shack near Haad Yao — fresh fruit shake and fried rice (80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Lamai Beach food market — mixed street food feast including satay, spring rolls, grilled fish, and fresh fruit (150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Phangan is famous for the Full Moon Party (check dates — if it falls on your visit, expect higher prices and crowds). The island has beautiful, quiet areas away from the party scene. Return ferries to Koh Samui run until around 17:00–18:00.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Samui — wake up for one last sunrise on the beach. Visit the Nathon Town market (Koh Samui's main town) for the most authentic and affordable local food experience on the island. Browse the fresh produce market and pick up Thai snacks and souvenirs to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, spend the final afternoon relaxing on the beach or visiting any remaining sights. Visit the Secret Buddha Garden (Magic Garden) — a quirky hillside garden with stone statues (entry ~80 THB, accessible by motorbike or taxi). Head to the airport or ferry pier for your onward journey.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Koh Samui or travel to Bangkok for international connections. If time allows before departure, enjoy one final Thai street food meal — make it count!

meals.breakfast: Nathon Town fresh market — local Thai breakfast of rice porridge, fried dough (pa thong ko), and Thai iced tea (50–70 THB)
meals.lunch: Final street food meal — choose your favorites from the trip: pad thai, green curry, mango sticky rice (100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport food court or grab snacks for the journey (100–150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time for transfers — getting from Koh Samui to Bangkok or international connections requires a ferry + flight or long bus journey. Book return transport in advance. Don't forget to declare any food items at customs. Budget summary: average daily spend should be 600–900 THB (approximately $17–25 USD) excluding accommodation and major transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Phuket International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and collect luggage, then arrange private transfer or shared minivan to Rassada Pier (approx. 45 min). Board the afternoon ferry to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check in to your Boutique Stay on Phi Phi Don and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Take a gentle stroll along the Tonsai Village beachfront to get your bearings. Watch the sunset from the beach and soak in the island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport — grab a Thai rice porridge (Jok) or a snack at the terminal.
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a pier-side café near Rassada Pier — try a Pad Thai or fried rice for around 80–120 THB.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Tonsai Village such as Papaya Restaurant — order Massaman curry and grilled fish for approximately 250–400 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance online or at the pier. The last ferry from Rassada to Phi Phi typically departs around 17:00–17:30, so aim to arrive at the pier by 16:00. October is shoulder season — expect occasional rain showers but generally good weather.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise hike up to Phi Phi Viewpoint (Koh Phi Phi Don Viewpoint). The 20–30 minute uphill trek rewards you with a breathtaking panoramic view over both bays. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling and island-hopping longtail boat tour departing from Tonsai Bay. Visit Maya Bay (The Beach), Pileh Lagoon, Viking Cave, and Monkey Beach. Snorkel amid vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village. Browse the lively night market stalls along the main walking street for souvenirs and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — fresh fruit, toast, and coffee for around 150 THB.
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack or eat at a beach shack near Maya Bay — grilled corn, fresh coconut, or a simple sandwich.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Tonsai Walking Street — try Pad Kra Pao (basil stir-fry), mango sticky rice, and fresh fruit shakes for 150–250 THB total.

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has regulated visitor quotas — book your boat tour early through your hotel to secure a spot. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. Snorkeling gear is usually provided on tours.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from Tonsai Beach and paddle around the dramatic limestone cliffs and hidden lagoons of Phi Phi Don at your own pace. Explore sea caves accessible only by kayak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Long Beach (Hat Yao), the quietest and most pristine beach on Phi Phi Don, reachable by a 15-minute walk or short longtail ride from Tonsai. Swim, sunbathe, and unwind.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Thai cooking class offered by local guesthouses in Tonsai Village (book in advance). Learn to make Tom Yum soup, green curry, and Pad Thai.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl or banana pancakes at a café on the Tonsai walking street — approximately 120–180 THB.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Long Beach — fresh grilled seafood skewers and coconut water from a beach vendor for 200–300 THB.
meals.dinner: Your cooking class meal IS dinner — enjoy the dishes you prepared together with fellow travelers.

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes on Phi Phi typically cost 800–1,200 THB per person and last 2–3 hours. Kayak rentals run approximately 200–300 THB per hour. Long Beach is calmer and less crowded than Tonsai — ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning longtail boat to Koh Phi Phi Leh (the uninhabited island) for a private sunrise experience before the crowds arrive. Explore Pileh Lagoon and Viking Cave up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don and check out of your boutique hotel. Board the afternoon ferry to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hrs). Check in to a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel in Krabi Town.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's famous Chao Fah Pier Night Market. Browse dozens of street food stalls, local crafts, and fresh seafood grills along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel — fruit, yogurt, and coffee before the boat trip.
meals.lunch: Lunch on return to Phi Phi — eat at a local warung (small eatery) in Tonsai for a simple rice dish around 80–120 THB.
meals.dinner: Feast at Krabi Night Market — grilled prawns, papaya salad, satay skewers, and Thai iced tea for 150–300 THB total.

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Phi Phi to Krabi depart multiple times daily. Book tickets the day before. Krabi Town is a great base for exploring Railay Beach, the Four Islands, and Tiger Cave Temple.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Wat Tham Suea (Tiger Cave Temple) — climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for a spectacular 360-degree view over Krabi Province. Start early to avoid heat. A golden Buddha and monk meditation caves await.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat from Krabi Town to the legendary Railay Beach (30-minute ride), accessible only by boat due to towering limestone cliffs. Explore Railay West and East beaches, and walk to Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of Thailand's most beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Railay West Beach, then return by longtail boat to Krabi Town. Enjoy a relaxed riverside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai breakfast at a local Krabi Town café — rice soup, fried egg, and Thai tea for 100–150 THB.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant on Railay — fresh seafood platter or green curry for 250–400 THB.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Krabi Town — try steamed sea bass with lime and chili for 300–450 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Tiger Cave Temple entry is free but a donation is appreciated. Start the climb before 8:00 AM to beat the heat. Longtail boats to Railay cost approximately 100 THB per person each way from Chao Fah Pier.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day Four Islands boat tour from Krabi Town. Visit Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tub, and Koh Mor — snorkeling, swimming, and beachcombing at each stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands tour — enjoy a picnic lunch on a sandbar that appears only at low tide connecting Koh Tub and Koh Mor. Snorkel the crystal-clear waters around Koh Poda.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by late afternoon. Visit the Krabi Walking Street (open on weekends) or relax with a traditional Thai massage at a local spa.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby bakery — croissant, fresh juice, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Included picnic lunch on the sandbar as part of the Four Islands tour — typically Thai rice boxes with fruit.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Krabi's local restaurant strip — Khao Soi (Northern Thai curry noodles) and spring rolls for 200–300 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Four Islands tours cost approximately 600–900 THB per person including snorkeling gear and lunch. Book through your hotel or a reputable local tour operator. Tide timing affects the sandbar — confirm with your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry or minivan + ferry combination (approx. 2 hrs). Check in to a mid-range beachfront bungalow or boutique resort on Koh Lanta's Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on Long Beach — one of Koh Lanta's longest and most serene stretches of sand. Rent a bicycle (100 THB/day) and explore the northern part of the island at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) on the east coast — a historic Sino-Portuguese fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses, local galleries, and atmospheric waterfront cafés.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast before departure in Krabi — grab a roti with banana and condensed milk from a street cart for 50–80 THB.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a Long Beach shack — grilled fish with rice and som tum (papaya salad) for 150–250 THB.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Old Town — fresh seafood at a waterfront restaurant overlooking the mangroves for 300–500 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Krabi to Koh Lanta run seasonally — confirm schedules in advance. October is early season for Koh Lanta, so the island is quieter and more affordable. Scooter rental (250–350 THB/day) is the best way to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter and ride south to Koh Lanta National Park (entry 200 THB). Trek through jungle trails to a lighthouse with panoramic views, explore mangrove boardwalks, and relax on the secluded park beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Khlong Nin Beach — a quieter, more bohemian stretch of Koh Lanta with chilled-out beach bars, hammocks, and a laid-back vibe. Swim and lounge the afternoon away.
day_by_day.evening: Return north along the west coast road as the sun sets — the drive itself offers stunning views. Enjoy a beachfront barbecue dinner near your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your resort — tropical fruit platter, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside café at Khlong Nin Beach — veggie curry or grilled prawns for 200–300 THB.
meals.dinner: Beachfront BBQ restaurant near Long Beach — mixed seafood grill with sticky rice for 350–500 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta National Park is open daily 8:00 AM–6:00 PM. The lighthouse trail is moderately easy and takes about 30 minutes. Wear sunscreen and bring insect repellent for the mangrove walk.

day_by_day.morning: Join a snorkeling day trip to the Koh Lanta Marine Park — visit Koh Rok (famous for its turquoise lagoon and vibrant coral) and Koh Ha (five interconnected islands with excellent snorkeling and diving).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the marine park tour — snorkel the shallow reefs of Koh Ha and enjoy a floating lunch on the boat. Spot sea turtles, reef sharks, and colorful marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage on the beach (300–400 THB/hr) and watch the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your resort before the tour departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch included on the boat tour — Thai rice boxes and fresh fruit.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Thai restaurant in the Saladan area — tom kha gai (coconut chicken soup) and pad see ew for 200–350 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok and Koh Ha trips cost approximately 1,200–1,800 THB per person. Koh Rok is further and more pristine — highly recommended. Book through your hotel the day before. Visibility is typically excellent in October.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Koh Lanta by ferry to Koh Phi Phi (approx. 1.5 hrs) or travel north to Ao Nang / Krabi for onward transfer to Koh Yao Noi — a peaceful, less-touristed island in Phang Nga Bay. Check in to a mid-range eco-resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Yao Noi by bicycle or scooter — visit the local fishing village, rubber plantations, and the stunning viewpoint overlooking Phang Nga Bay's limestone karsts.
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset kayaking tour through the mangroves and sea caves of Phang Nga Bay — paddle past dramatic karst formations as the sky turns orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast on the ferry or at Krabi pier — roti with egg and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local village restaurant on Koh Yao Noi — simple Thai home cooking (khao man gai or curry) for 80–150 THB.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your eco-resort restaurant — fresh catch of the day with jasmine rice and stir-fried vegetables for 300–450 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Yao Noi is accessible by longtail boat from Bang Rong Pier near Phuket (30 min) or from Krabi. It's a Muslim fishing community — dress modestly when visiting the village. This island offers an authentic, crowd-free Thai island experience.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day Phang Nga Bay tour by traditional longtail boat — visit the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), Ko Panyi floating Muslim village, and dramatic limestone sea caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour — kayak through hidden hongs (collapsed cave chambers) accessible only at low tide. Swim in the emerald green waters surrounded by towering karsts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Yao Noi. Enjoy a quiet evening — stargaze from the beach away from city light pollution, or join a local fisherman for an evening fishing experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your eco-resort — Thai-style omelet, fruit, and herbal tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ko Panyi floating village — try the famous fresh seafood dishes served by village residents for 200–350 THB.
meals.dinner: BBQ dinner on the beach at your resort or a nearby beachfront spot — grilled fish and sticky rice for 300–400 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay tours from Koh Yao Noi cost approximately 1,000–1,500 THB per person. Ko Panyi is a fascinating floating village built on stilts — explore its mosque, school, and seafood restaurants. Book your tour the previous evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take the longtail boat from Koh Yao Noi to Bang Rong Pier and transfer to Phuket (approx. 1 hr total). Check in to a mid-range hotel in Patong or Kata Beach area. Freshen up and explore the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kata Beach or Karon Beach — two of Phuket's most beautiful and less chaotic beaches compared to Patong. Swim, paddleboard, or simply relax on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Patong's vibrant Bangla Road night scene — lively street food stalls, live music bars, and a bustling atmosphere. Experience the energy without overindulging.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before departure from Koh Yao Noi — fruit and coffee at your resort.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside café at Kata Beach — fish and chips or Thai green curry for 200–350 THB.
meals.dinner: Street food crawl on Bangla Road and surrounding streets — satay, grilled corn, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut for 200–300 THB total.

day_by_day.notes: Phuket is larger and more commercialized than the other islands visited — manage expectations accordingly. Kata and Karon beaches are far more pleasant than Patong Beach for swimming. Use a metered taxi or Grab app for getting around Phuket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Big Buddha (Phra Phuttha Ming Mongkol Akenakkiri) on Nakkerd Hill — a 45-meter white marble statue with sweeping views over southern Phuket. Dress respectfully (sarongs available to borrow).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — stroll the Sino-Portuguese streets of Thalang Road and Soi Romanee, visit colorful shophouses, street art murals, and local museums. Stop at the weekend market if available.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Thailand — enjoy a special farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Phuket Old Town or a beachfront fine dining spot. Reflect on the journey and pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Phuket Old Town café — kaya toast, soft-boiled eggs, and strong Thai coffee (kopi) for 100–150 THB.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Old Town — try Mee Hokkien (Hokkien noodles) or O-Tao (oyster omelet) for 100–180 THB.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range rooftop restaurant in Phuket Old Town — Thai tasting menu with fresh seafood, curries, and desserts for 500–800 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: Big Buddha is free to visit but donations are welcomed. Phuket Old Town is walkable and best explored on foot. If departing the next morning, arrange airport transfer in advance — Phuket Airport is approximately 45 minutes from Kata/Patong area. Consider booking a late checkout to freshen up before your flight.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to pier, followed by a luxury speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique stay, unwind with a welcome drink, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront promenade to soak in the turquoise waters and lush limestone karst scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace or beach bar overlooking the Andaman Sea. Gentle orientation walk through Tonsai Village to discover the vibrant night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — en route to Phi Phi Islands
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi — a beloved fine-casual spot serving elevated Thai and Mediterranean dishes; try the fresh grilled barracuda with lemongrass and the massaman lamb curry

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private speedboat transfer in advance for comfort and speed. October is shoulder season — expect occasional rain showers but fewer crowds and lush green scenery. Keep essentials in carry-on for easy access upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat sunrise tour around Phi Phi Leh — visit the iconic Maya Bay (arrive early before crowds), snorkel in Pileh Lagoon's crystal-clear emerald waters, and explore Viking Cave with its ancient paintings and swiftlet nests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don for a guided cliff-top hike to the Phi Phi Viewpoint for panoramic views of both bays. Relax on Loh Dalum Bay beach with a private cabana setup arranged by the hotel, complete with chilled towels and fresh coconuts.
day_by_day.evening: Fire show on the beach followed by a private candlelit seafood dinner on the sand.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — tropical fruit platters, eggs Benedict, freshly pressed juices and Thai-style congee with ginger and century egg
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Ciao Bella — fresh grilled prawns, som tum papaya salad, and coconut ice cream
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner arranged by the hotel — whole grilled lobster, steamed sea bass with lime and chili, sticky rice with mango for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has timed entry restrictions to protect the ecosystem — confirm permits with the hotel concierge the evening before. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Island hopping by private speedboat to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — a pristine, largely uninhabited island with powder-white sand and shallow turquoise waters ideal for swimming and snorkeling among colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for world-class snorkeling with vibrant coral gardens and sea turtles. Enjoy a luxury picnic lunch on a secluded beach prepared by the hotel's kitchen team.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don. Enjoy a traditional Thai massage at a premium spa on the island — opt for a 90-minute herbal compress and aromatherapy oil massage.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — freshly baked croissants, smoked salmon, tropical fruit, and barista-crafted coffee
meals.lunch: Luxury picnic on Koh Yung beach — cold-pressed juices, artisan sandwiches, Thai spring rolls, fresh fruit, and dark chocolate truffles
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Cove Restaurant — upscale Thai cuisine with panoramic sea views; recommended dishes include Panang curry with wagyu beef and steamed jasmine rice

day_by_day.notes: Bring waterproof bags for electronics during the speedboat ride. October waters are generally calm but can have swells — motion sickness tablets recommended if sensitive.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning yoga session on the hotel's beach deck at sunrise, led by a resident instructor. Follow with a guided kayaking excursion through the sea caves and hidden lagoons along Phi Phi's eastern coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Phi Phi Natural Education Center to learn about marine conservation efforts and coral restoration programs. Participate in a guided reef-check snorkel with a marine biologist.
day_by_day.evening: Street food evening tour of Tonsai Village — guided walk sampling local delicacies including pad kra pao (basil stir-fry), roti with banana and condensed milk, fresh sugarcane juice, and mango sticky rice from market stalls.

meals.breakfast: Light in-hotel breakfast — acai bowls, granola, yogurt, and green smoothies to prepare for yoga
meals.lunch: Lunch at Papaya Restaurant — authentic Thai home cooking; order the tom yum goong (spicy shrimp soup) and pad see ew with fresh crab
meals.dinner: Street food tour serves as dinner — curated tastings across 6–8 local vendors in Tonsai Village

day_by_day.notes: The street food tour is best experienced with a local guide who can navigate the best stalls and explain dishes. Carry small Thai baht notes for market purchases. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat transfer to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours). Morning visit to the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking 360-degree views over Krabi Province and the Andaman coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krabi Town's vibrant weekend walking street market area and visit the Chao Fah Pier mangrove forest by kayak — paddle through ancient mangrove tunnels teeming with wildlife including monitor lizards and exotic birds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Islands by private speedboat. Sunset dinner at the hotel with a curated tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Thai breakfast including jok (rice porridge), fried eggs with oyster sauce, and fresh tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Lunch at Krabi Town's Ruan Mai Restaurant — a legendary local institution; try the crab fried rice and stir-fried morning glory with garlic
meals.dinner: In-hotel tasting menu dinner — 5-course Thai fusion menu with wine pairing, featuring dishes like blue swimmer crab bisque, duck red curry, and pandan panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — start early to avoid midday heat. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) as it is an active temple. Carry plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat to the Railay Beach peninsula — accessible only by boat, this stunning enclave features four distinct beaches. Begin at Railay West for a morning swim, then walk through to Railay East and Phra Nang Cave Beach, famous for its princess shrine and dramatic limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing session on Railay's world-famous limestone karsts with a certified instructor — suitable for all levels. Alternatively, explore Phra Nang Cave and the hidden lagoon trail for a jungle adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a clifftop bar, then return by speedboat to Phi Phi for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs your way, fresh pastries, tropical fruit, and specialty Thai iced tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Railay Beach Bar & Restaurant — beachfront dining with fresh seafood; try the grilled tiger prawns with garlic butter and green papaya salad
meals.dinner: Dinner at Phi Phi's Cosmic Restaurant — international and Thai fusion menu; recommended are the red curry risotto and whole fried snapper with sweet chili sauce

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by longtail or speedboat — no road access. Tides affect beach access at Railay East; check tide times with the hotel concierge. Rock climbing helmets and harnesses are provided by the instructor.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private luxury yacht charter departing from Phi Phi. Morning sail to the stunning four-island cluster — Koh Mook (Emerald Cave), Koh Kradan, Koh Libong, and Koh Cheung. Swim through the sea tunnel into Emerald Cave's hidden inland beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor off Koh Kradan — rated one of Thailand's most beautiful islands. Snorkel over pristine coral gardens, sunbathe on the immaculate white sand beach, and enjoy a gourmet lunch served on deck by the yacht's crew.
day_by_day.evening: Sail back toward Phi Phi at sunset with champagne on deck. Return to the boutique stay for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — continental spread with fresh-baked breads, cold cuts, tropical fruits, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-deck yacht lunch — seared tuna tartare, lobster rolls, chilled white wine, fresh fruit platter, and artisan cheeses
meals.dinner: Dinner at Phi Phi's Le Grand Bleu — French-Thai fusion restaurant; standout dishes include bouillabaisse with local seafood and coconut crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private yacht charters should be booked at least 3–5 days in advance through the hotel concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light layers for the sea breeze. Champagne and snorkeling equipment are typically included in premium charters.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation morning — indulge in a 2-hour luxury spa journey at the hotel's wellness center: begin with a traditional Thai herbal steam bath, followed by a full-body scrub using local turmeric and coconut, and finish with a hot stone massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Phi Phi Don photography walk — hire a local photography guide to capture the island's most photogenic spots including the twin bays viewpoint, colorful longtail boats, and the bustling village market. Alternatively, take a free afternoon to swim, read, and relax at the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Private Thai cooking class on the beach — learn to prepare 4 signature dishes including tom kha gai (coconut galangal soup), green curry, mango sticky rice, and fresh spring rolls with a local chef.

meals.breakfast: Light spa-prep breakfast — green smoothie bowl, chia pudding, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Lunch at the hotel's beach restaurant — fresh catch of the day, grilled with herbs, served with jasmine rice and stir-fried vegetables
meals.dinner: The dishes prepared in your cooking class become your dinner — enjoyed at a beachside table with a bottle of chilled Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a highly memorable experience — request a market visit component to shop for fresh ingredients with the chef before cooking. Photography guide can double as a cultural storyteller for deeper local insight.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private speedboat to Koh Lanta — a larger, more laid-back island approximately 1.5 hours from Phi Phi. Visit the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a historic Chinese-Malay fishing village with stilted wooden shophouses, art galleries, and artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta's pristine west coast beaches — Klong Dao Beach and Long Beach are particularly beautiful. Visit the Mu Ko Lanta National Park for a short jungle trek to spot wildlife and visit the lighthouse at the island's southern tip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi by private speedboat. Quiet evening at the hotel with a nightcap at the bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread including dim sum bites, fresh fruit, and Thai-style omelette with oyster sauce
meals.lunch: Lunch at Koh Lanta's Same Same But Different Restaurant — creative Thai and international fusion; try the soft-shell crab tacos and coconut curry noodles
meals.dinner: Dinner at Phi Phi's Outrigger Restaurant — beachfront setting, fresh seafood barbecue platter for two with dipping sauces and sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta Old Town is a UNESCO-listed heritage site — respectful photography is appreciated. The national park entrance fee is minimal. Wear sturdy shoes for the lighthouse trek.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated beach morning at Long Beach (Hat Yao) on Phi Phi Don — the island's longest and most pristine stretch of sand. Arrange a private beach setup through the hotel with sun loungers, a parasol, chilled towels, and a cooler of refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underwater photography or freediving experience — hire a certified instructor for a 3-hour session exploring Phi Phi's vibrant reef systems. Alternatively, take a stand-up paddleboard lesson in the calm bay waters.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-celebration dinner at the finest restaurant on the island — dress up for a special evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, freshly squeezed orange juice, and a selection of tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch delivered to your private setup — club sandwiches, fresh spring rolls, coconut water, and fruit skewers
meals.dinner: Dinner at Phi Phi's Hippies Bar & Restaurant — elevated atmosphere with live acoustic music; enjoy the whole grilled lobster, wagyu beef massaman curry, and passion fruit soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Freediving sessions require a brief health declaration form — inform the hotel concierge of any medical conditions. October sea visibility can vary; the instructor will advise on the best dive sites for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Morning excursion to Monkey Beach (Hat Ling) — a small cove accessible by longtail boat, home to resident macaque monkeys. Observe the wildlife responsibly (do not feed the monkeys) and enjoy the dramatic scenery of the surrounding cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a leisurely afternoon. Browse the local boutique shops and artisan stalls in Tonsai Village for Thai silk scarves, hand-painted ceramics, and locally made jewelry. Visit the Phi Phi Island Village for a cultural craft demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfire night — the hotel arranges a private beachfire with cocktails, acoustic guitar, and a platter of Thai tapas under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Thai breakfast with khao tom (rice soup), fried egg, pickled vegetables, and jasmine tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local shophouse restaurant in Tonsai Village — authentic pad thai, fresh spring rolls, and Thai iced coffee
meals.dinner: In-hotel private beachfire dinner — Thai tapas including satay skewers, fish cakes, miang kham leaf wraps, and coconut pudding dessert

day_by_day.notes: Monkey Beach is best visited in the morning when macaques are most active. Keep bags closed and avoid direct eye contact with the monkeys. The beachfire evening should be reserved with the hotel at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final island adventure — private snorkeling and free-diving tour to Phi Phi's most remote reef systems, including Hin Phae and Bida Nok — renowned for leopard sharks, black-tip reef sharks, and abundant tropical fish. Depart early for the best underwater visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a final relaxation afternoon. Indulge in a couple's or solo 60-minute aromatherapy massage at the spa. Pack and prepare for departure. Enjoy a final swim and sunset from the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner — the hotel's chef prepares a bespoke 7-course tasting menu reflecting the flavors of your journey through Thailand, paired with curated wines.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full continental and Thai spread; savor every bite of your last morning
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel pool bar — fresh ceviche, grilled vegetable skewers, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Bespoke 7-course farewell tasting menu at the hotel — highlights include chilled prawn bisque, steamed sea bass in banana leaf, duck leg red curry, artisan cheese course, and lychee sorbet with rose water

day_by_day.notes: Arrange checkout logistics and departure transfer with the hotel concierge this evening. Confirm speedboat timing to the pier and onward transport to the airport for Day 13. Allow extra time for any last-minute shopping or packing.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beach — a quiet, reflective moment to take in the beauty of Phi Phi Islands one last time. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the hotel before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer from Phi Phi Islands to Krabi or Phuket pier (depending on departure flight). Airport transfer via private air-conditioned vehicle. Time at the airport lounge before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry home memories of pristine beaches, vibrant coral reefs, exquisite Thai cuisine, and the warm hospitality of the Andaman coast.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — your choice of Thai or Western; indulge in one last mango sticky rice or eggs Benedict
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a quick stop at a premium airport restaurant — try a final bowl of tom yum soup or pad see ew before boarding
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 12:00 noon — arrange a late checkout or luggage storage with the hotel if the speedboat departs later. Confirm all bookings, receipts, and travel documents the night before. Tip service staff generously — it is customary and deeply appreciated in Thai culture.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
